chunks: First: Ali ibn Mahziyar said: I said to him, 'Some of your mawalis have narrated from your fathers (peace be upon them) that every waqf (endowment) to a known time is obligatory upon the heirs, and every waqf to an unknown, ignorant time is invalid upon the heirs. And you are more knowledgeable about the opinion of your fathers.' So he wrote: 'It is as I said.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said:

The waqf is valid as long as it is perpetual, according to the earlier narrations in the first chapter which include the condition of the deed of waqf. And if it is not perpetual, it is not valid in any case.

The meaning in this report is that his saying 'every waqf to a known time' means that if the object of the waqf is mentioned, because if he does not mention the object of the waqf in the endowment, the waqf becomes invalid. And he did not mean by 'time' the fixed term (age), and this was a convention among them.

And that which indicates this is what Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated, who said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) asking him about the waqf that is valid, how is it? For it has been narrated that the waqf, if it is not timed, is invalid and returned to the heirs, and if it is timed, it is valid.

Then some people said: The timed one is the one who mentions in it that it is a waqf for so-and-so and his descendants, and when they perish, it is for the poor and the needy until Allah (Exalted and Mighty) inherits the earth and whoever is on it.

And others said: This is timed if he mentions that it is for so-and-so and his descendants as long as they remain, and he does not mention at the end for the poor and the needy until Allah inherits the earth and whoever is on it.
And that which is not timed is that he says: 'This is a waqf' and does not mention anyone. So which of these is valid and which is invalid?
So he wrote: The endowments are according to what one endows, if Allah wills.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a valid Islamic waqf (endowment) regarding perpetuity and beneficiaries?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the jurisprudential debate among Shia scholars regarding the validity of *waqf* (endowment), specifically addressing whether it must be perpetual or if it can be time-bound. It highlights the distinction between a *waqf* that reverts to heirs upon the extinction of beneficiaries versus one that remains valid in perpetuity for the poor, reflecting the nuanced interpretations of Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his predecessors on the conditions of endowment contracts.
